title: 2021 Fall AMC 10B Problem 12
statement: Which of the following conditions is sufficient to guarantee that integers \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) satisfy the equation \[x(x-y)+y(y-z)+z(z-x) \]\[= 1?\]

solutions.text:
Let \(E=x(x-y)+y(y-z)\) \(+z(z-x).\) Expanding gives \[ \begin{aligned} 2E={}&(x-y)^2+(y-z)^2\\ &+(z-x)^2. \end{aligned} \]

For the value to be \(1,\) the three nonnegative square terms must sum to \(2.\) Since \(x,y,z\) are integers, this means the squared differences are \(1,1,0.\)

Thus two of the variables must be equal, and the third must differ from them by \(1.\) The condition \(x=z\) and \(y-1=x\) guarantees exactly that.

Thus, the answer is D .
